purpose: Independent practice of C1.2 and C1.4 — translating a pattern across three representations (shapes, numbers, table of values) AND using the table to predict a faraway term with whole numbers up to 1000.
student_learning_goal: I can build a table of values for a number pattern up to 1000 and use it to predict a faraway term.

parts.part_title: Part 2: Find the missing far value
parts.student_instructions: Fill in the missing value AND write the rule. Then predict term 20 using the rule. Justify your reasoning on the lines.
parts.visual_layout: A 2-column table with headers TERM and VALUE. 5 data rows: TERM 1, 2, 3, 4, 10. VALUE 50, 100, 150, 200, ___. Below the table: 'Rule: +____.' Below: 'Term 20 = ____' Below that: 'How did you figure out term 20?' on three writing lines.

parts.answer_key: Missing value (term 10) = 500. Rule = +50. Term 20 = 1000 (computed as 20 × 50 = 1000, using the term × N shortcut for a +N rule starting at N). Justification: 'Each value is term × 50, so term 20 = 20 × 50 = 1000.' Accept skip-counting as a valid alternative ('I added 50 ten more times to 500 to get 1000.').

parts.part_title: Part 3: Build all three reps yourself
parts.student_instructions: Pick your own +N rule with N between 25 and 100. Build all three reps. Then predict term 10 AND term 20. Decide if your rule will reach more than 1000 — at what term?
parts.visual_layout: Top: 'My rule: +____. Start at ____.' Three workspaces: (1) An empty 5-cell shape parade strip labelled 'My shape parade'. (2) A row of 5 empty boxes labelled 'My number sequence'. (3) An empty 2-column table with TERM (1-5 pre-filled) and VALUE (blank) labelled 'My table of values'. Bottom: 'Term 10 = ____. Term 20 = ____. Could term ___ ever be more than 1000? At what term: ___?'

parts.answer_key: All three reps must follow the same chosen rule. Examples: Rule +50 starting at 50 → term 10 = 500, term 20 = 1000, crosses 1000 at term 21. Rule +30 starting at 30 → term 10 = 300, term 20 = 600, crosses 1000 at term 34. Correct if the rule is preserved across all three reps AND the term predictions match the rule AND the ceiling reasoning is plausible.

early_finisher_prompt: If you finish, try Part 3 with a MULTIPLICATIVE rule (×2 or ×3). What happens to the values? At what term do they exceed 1000?
teacher_notes: Lesson 3 consolidation — KEYSTONE evidence. Watch for: (a) Part 1 children who fill the table correctly with TERM/VALUE headers — this is C1.2 evidence at L3. (b) Part 2 children who use the term × N shortcut to predict term 20 (multiplication) versus skip-counting are at L3+ on C1.3+C1.4. (c) Part 3 children who can identify the ceiling term (when values exceed 1000) are showing L4 generalization. Use Part 2 + Part 3 as primary evidence for the L3 formative tracker columns.
